title: Manipulating HTML Element Attributes
summary: Shows how to inspect an element's attributes with .attributes, read one with getAttribute and change one with setAttribute, using an anchor's href as the example.

concepts.heading: Attributes recap
points: An attribute is anything written inside an opening tag besides the tag name: class on most elements, href on anchors, src on images.
Attributes are the third thing you can change from JS after styles and text.

concepts.heading: Reading and changing attributes
points: element.attributes returns a collection of every attribute currently on the element. For a link with only an href, it holds one entry.
element.getAttribute('name') returns the value of one attribute as a string. The method name is singular and requires the attribute name as its argument, e.g. getAttribute('href').
element.setAttribute('name', 'value') takes two arguments: which attribute, and the new value. It overwrites the attribute if it exists and creates it otherwise.
Changing href redirects the click target, but the visible link text is separate (it comes from the content), so a link can still say Google while pointing elsewhere.
querySelector('a') returns only the first anchor on the page, so that is the one affected.
(Extra) The same pattern works for src, alt, id, class, disabled, etc. removeAttribute('name') deletes one, and hasAttribute('name') tests for it.

task.name: Redirect a link with setAttribute
task.starting_point: A page with a single anchor pointing to Google and a linked script.js.
task.goal: Point the link at a different site using JavaScript.
steps: Select the anchor and log its attributes.
Call setAttribute with 'href' and the new URL.
Click the link to confirm it goes to the new site although the text is unchanged.
task.expected_result: The link text is unchanged but the click lands on the new URL.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 16 - The Document Object Model (DOM)/16.07 - Manipulating HTML Element Attributes

pitfalls: Passing only one argument to setAttribute.
The reference repo has a typo in the URL (four w's) which should be www.
Forgetting that link text does not update when href changes.
